articles.title: A driver's time should earn more than the fuel it burns
articles.description: The case for sharing a journey without losing control of your day.
articles.coverAlt: A driver route connects available passenger seats. TagRides Shared Value, part one.
articles.takeaway: A shared journey should work for the person behind the wheel, after the costs of providing it.

articles.title: Getting around should leave room for a life
articles.description: School, business, appointments or time with family—a useful journey should fit your budget and your plans.
articles.coverAlt: A rider's amber path joins a shared teal journey. TagRides Shared Value, part two.
articles.takeaway: The useful fare is the one that makes the complete journey work—and still makes sense tomorrow.

articles.title: The next transport breakthrough may already have a seat
articles.description: What better use of existing journeys could mean for cities, the environment and the people investing in both.
articles.coverAlt: Shared routes connect with a wider transport network. TagRides Shared Value, part three.
articles.takeaway: The opportunity is more useful travel from existing capacity. The proof is what changes on real journeys.

city-map.webp.label: Captured on iOS
city-map.webp.title: Every connection starts in a real place.
city-map.webp.caption: The TagRides home screen around Yaba, captured on the iOS simulator on 25 September 2026. Map locations provide context, not an announced service area or public-transport integration.

driver-value.svg.caption: The driver's useful return is what remains after the relevant costs. An explanatory framework, not a forecast.

seat-model.svg.caption: Illustrative seat count: four offered places, two passengers boarded through the app and one place used outside it leave one available place. An accepted Along fare is not an advance reservation.

rider-priorities.svg.caption: Source: TagRides' early survey of 210 Lagos riders. Respondents could name several priorities; these are company-sample counts, not citywide estimates.

whole-journey.svg.caption: Compare the complete trip: shared-leg fare, connecting fares and relevant fees. Consider walking and waiting alongside the cash total.

impact-test.svg.caption: Three questions for assessing a shared ride's environmental effect. A measurement framework, not measured TagRides impact.

transit-connection.svg.caption: A possible feeder journey, shown schematically. No live bus service, ticket integration or fixed route is being announced.

repeat-value.svg.caption: A framework for evaluating the pilot: repeat riders, worthwhile driver earnings, dependable pickups and sustainable service costs.
